They together supply 50 MVAR to a 11 kV grid. Current supplied by both the machines is equal. Synchronous reactances of machine A and machine B are 1\(\Omega\) and 3\(\Omega\) respectively. Assuming the magnetic circuit to be linear, the ratio of excitation current of machine A to that of machine B is ______.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Two parallel connected, three-phase, 50Hz, 11kV, star-connected synchronous machines A and B, are operating as synchronous condensers. They together supply 50 MVAR to a 11 kV grid. Current supplied by both the machines is equal. Synchronous reactances of machine A and machine B are 1\(\Omega\) and 3\(\Omega\) respectively. Assuming the magnetic circuit to be linear, the ratio of excitation current of machine A to that of machine B is ______.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows two synchronous machines A and B connected in parallel to the 11 kV busbar, supplying 50 MVAR to the power grid. The A branch is marked with synchronous reactance 1 Ω, and the B branch is marked with synchronous reactance 3 Ω; the figure also gives the bus current calculation formula I_L = 50×10^6/(√3×11×10^3) = 2624.31 A. Then reason: three-phase reactive power satisfies Q = √3 V_LL I_L, so the bus current I_L = 50×10^6/(√3×11×10^3) = 2624.31 A. The problem states that the currents supplied by the two machines are equal, therefore the line current of each machine is 2624.31/2 = 1312.16 A. Since the two machines are star-connected, the line current is equal to the phase current, so the phase current of each machine I = 1312.16 A. The phase voltage V_ph = 11×10^3/√3 = 6350.85 V. When the synchronous condenser supplies reactive power to the system, according to the given method, use the per-phase potential relationship E = V_ph + X_s I. Thus the internal potential of machine A is E_A = 6350.85 + 1×1312.16 = 7663.01 V; the internal potential of machine B is E_B = 6350.85 + 3×1312.16 = 10287.33 V. When the magnetic circuit is linear, the excitation current is proportional to the internal potential, therefore I_fA/I_fB = E_A/E_B = 7663.01/10287.33 = 0.7448, approximately 0.74.
